newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: CRICKET-ZIMBABWE HOLD UP ENGLAND VICTORY PUSH.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ZIMBABWE HOLD UP ENGLAND VICTORY PUSH.

text.p: Andy Waller hit his maiden test half-century to help Zimbabwe hold up England's push for victory on the fifth and final day of the first test at Queen's Club on Sunday.
Zimbabwe, 107 for five overnight, were hanging on grimly at 188 for seven at lunch, a lead of 158 with two sessions remaining.
England made the best possible start by getting rid of nightwatchman Bryan Strang in the third over of the morning.
Strang tried to heave the left-arm spin of Phil Tufnell over long on but succeeded only in hitting the ball straight up in the air toAlan Mullally at mid-on.
The touring side were then frustrated by a seventh wicket stand of 67 between 37-year-old test debutant Waller and all-rounder Guy Whittall.
Waller reached a fine 50 with his fifth four, having also hit two sixes in a stay of 106 deliveries.

However, three balls later Darren Gough found some extra bounce and Waller, trying to fend the ball down, succeeded only in edging it to be caught by Nick Knight at first slip without adding to his score.
Whittall was unbeaten at lunch on 37 with Paul Strang on five.
